english.title: Fail to comply Article 38(1) when transporting waste destined for recovery in non-EU country where OECD decision applies
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) transported waste specified in Article 38(1) of the Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council on shipments of waste, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE WASTE..), destined for recovery in a non-EU country to which the OECD Decision applied, namely **(..SPECIFY THE COUNTRY..), without the provisions of that Article having been complied with, in that **(..SPECIFY THE BREACH..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 24(2)(a) and 58 of the Transfrontier Shipment of Waste Regulations 2007.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
transport waste specified in Article 38(1) of Regulation (EC) 1013/2006
destined for recovery in a non-EU country to which the OECD decision applied
without the provisions of that Article having been complied with

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
